newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian government pushing through MMT ban bill.
newsitem.headline: Canadian government pushing through MMT ban bill.

text.p: The Canadian Parliament passed a government motion on Wednesday to cut off debate on a bill that will effectively ban the controversial gasoline additive MMT.
Debate on the bill, which opposition parties had held up with continual amendments, will be limited to three hours on the day the bill next comes up for consideration in the House of Commons.
After debate is finished, the bill will be voted on and then, if passed, proceed directly to the unelected Senate for ratification.

Although the bill is not currently on the government's Projected Order of Business, a spokeswoman for Environment Minister Sergio Marchi said she expected the bill would be passed "within the next week."
The official opposition, the Bloc Quebecois, reacted strongly to the introduction of closure, the motion used by the Liberal government to curtail debate.
"The Liberals wish to have their bill so much that they are defying the most elementary rules of democracy," Monique Guay, the Bloc's environment spokeswoman, said in a news release.
The bill, if passed, would ban the import of and interprovincial trade in MMT, methylcyclopentadienyl manganese tricarbonyl.
MMT is an octane enhancer, but both automakers and environmentalists back the ban, arguing it gums up car diagnostic systems and risks damaging people's health.
It is made by Ethyl Corp and imported into Canada by its subsidiary, Ethyl Canada. It used to be banned but is now allowed in the United States.
